ground_truth.description: Stage 2 is told to record over-cap and outage-deferred UUIDs under stats key `entity_refresh_retried_deferred` "so the next cycle can pick them up," but the only channel Stage 2 consumes is Stage 1's `entity_refresh_failed_uuids`. Stage 1 only records freshly-failed refreshes into that key and never re-reads a prior Stage 2's `entity_refresh_retried_deferred`, so deferred/over-cap UUIDs are silently dropped and never actually retried in a later cycle.

The 3-consecutive-error abort and the 20-UUID cap both dump remaining UUIDs into `entity_refresh_retried_deferred`, but an errored UUID is also added to `entity_refresh_retried_failed` (step 3); the prompt does not disambiguate whether the UUID that triggered the 3rd consecutive error belongs to `retried_failed`, `retried_deferred`, or both, allowing double-counting or omission depending on interpretation.

The new contract test only exercises `_format_report` serialization of the stats key; it does not verify that Stage 1 actually writes `entity_refresh_failed_uuids` on an error response, nor that Stage 2 reads and retries them, so the core producer/consumer behavior claimed by the change remains untested.

task.title: Stage 1 system prompt: record entity_uuid in stats on refresh_entity_summary failure
task.description:
Stage 1 (memory_consolidator) does not log the entity UUID when refresh_entity_summary fails with NodeNotFoundError or other errors. This was discovered in cycle-46 remediation (Stage 2 run 1f8c7813): the refresh failure left no recoverable record of the target entity, requiring heuristic identification in remediation. The next remediation cycle could not precisely target the failed entity.

Required fix: update the Stage 1 system prompt to mandate that on any refresh_entity_summary failure, the attempted entity_uuid is recorded in the cycle stats dict as `entity_refresh_failed_uuid` (or appended to an `entity_refresh_failed_uuids` list), OR emit a brief Mem0 observation containing the UUID so the next remediation cycle can target it precisely. This prevents the "UUID recovery by heuristic" pattern that cost a full reconciliation cycle.
task.details:
Source: Stage 2 remediation run 1f8c7813-ef60-4cc3-b2cc-921c4d487ee5, finding_id=2 (procedural_gap, severity=minor).

Stage 1 report context: Stage 1 run that triggered this had `entity_refreshes_attempted=2, entity_refreshes_succeeded=2` reported in stats, but cycle-46 showed a failure case where no UUID was recoverable from the run record. The existing `entity_refresh_failed_uuid` key (if not present) should be added to the stats dict format in the Stage 1 prompt.

Implementation: In the Stage 1 system prompt section that describes refresh_entity_summary calls, add an explicit rule: "On NodeNotFoundError or any other exception from refresh_entity_summary, write the attempted entity_uuid into the stats dict under entity_refresh_failed_uuids (append to list). If stats are already finalized, emit a one-sentence add_memory(category=observations_and_summaries) with the UUID so Stage 2 can locate it."

Companion tasks: 1145 (Stage 1 temporal-fact write-path migration), 1144 (Stage 1 UUID resolution before delete_memory calls).

plan.analysis:
Task 1157 mandates that Stage 1 (Memory Consolidator) records the attempted entity_uuid whenever `refresh_entity_summary` raises (NodeNotFoundError or any other exception), so the next remediation cycle can target the failed entity precisely instead of recovering it heuristically. The Stage 1 reconciliation harness emits the entity_refreshes_attempted/entity_refreshes_succeeded counters today but discards the attempted UUID on failure, leaving the cycle-46 remediation gap noted in Stage 2 run 1f8c7813-ef60-4cc3-b2cc-921c4d487ee5 finding 2.

The fix is a system-prompt-only change. Stage 1's behaviour is enforced by an LLM agent reading `STAGE1_SYSTEM_PROMPT`; production Python code does not write the new key directly. We therefore add a new "## Refresh Entity Summary Failure Recording" section to `STAGE1_SYSTEM_PROMPT` that (a) names the canonical stats key `entity_refresh_failed_uuids` (list, append on each failure), and (b) provides the post-finalisation fallback: emit a one-sentence `add_memory(category='observations_and_summaries')` containing the UUID so Stage 2 can locate it.

PREMISE NOTE: The two file paths the task description lists are slightly off — `fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/stage1.py` does not exist; the actual prompt module is `prompts/stage1.py` (verified by Read). Similarly, `tests/reconciliation/test_stage1.py` exists but is scoped to project_root threading (task 1174); the natural home for prompt-content existence checks is `tests/test_refresh_entity_summary.py` where the existing `TestStage1PromptMentionsRefreshEntitySummary` class already pins the refresh_entity_summary mentions in STAGE1_SYSTEM_PROMPT (single-line `assert 'refresh_entity_summary' in STAGE1_SYSTEM_PROMPT` style). The plan therefore edits the real prompt module and adds the test to the natural home (recorded as design decision below).

TEST SCOPE: This is a documentation/prompt-content change — the prompt is a string constant whose content drives LLM behaviour at runtime. Per the architect rules, doc-prose pinning via long substring/regex tests is forbidden, but a one-line existence check on a load-bearing canonical token (the new stats key) is allowed and matches the existing `TestStage1PromptMentionsRefreshEntitySummary` precedent and the task 1192 review consensus. We add exactly one such existence check on `entity_refresh_failed_uuids` — the machine-readable contract token Stage 2 remediation will eventually grep for. No tests on full sentences, ordering, or section titles.

REUSE: We extend (not replace) the existing `TestStage1PromptMentionsRefreshEntitySummary` class at tests/test_refresh_entity_summary.py:851 with one additional sibling test method, mirroring the surrounding pattern. The prompt edit follows the section template established by the "## UUID Resolution Discipline" (task 1144 step-1) and "## Verifying update_edge writes (Task 1145 Guard 2)" sections — heading line, short rationale, numbered procedure, optional fallback clause.

OUT OF SCOPE: stats_verifier.py changes — `_OP_TO_STAT` keys are integer counters, while `entity_refresh_failed_uuids` is a list of UUIDs the LLM populates directly into stats. The verifier overwrites integer counts from observed write_journal ops; adding a list-typed key would require a separate verifier extension. Per task description ("update the Stage 1 system prompt to mandate ..."), the scope is prompt-only.

design_decisions.decision: Edit `prompts/stage1.py` (not the non-existent `reconciliation/stage1.py` listed in the task brief), and add the new test to `tests/test_refresh_entity_summary.py` (not `tests/reconciliation/test_stage1.py` listed in the task brief).
design_decisions.rationale: Premise verification showed the task description's file paths are off. STAGE1_SYSTEM_PROMPT actually lives at `prompts/stage1.py` (`reconciliation/stage1.py` does not exist). The natural test home is `tests/test_refresh_entity_summary.py:851` (`TestStage1PromptMentionsRefreshEntitySummary`), which already contains existence checks for refresh_entity_summary content in STAGE1_SYSTEM_PROMPT. Putting the new test in `tests/reconciliation/test_stage1.py` (which is scoped to project_root payload threading per task 1174) would split the prompt-content pin away from its natural cluster. Companion task 1144 (UUID Resolution Discipline) also edited `prompts/stage1.py`, confirming this is the canonical location.

design_decisions.decision: Test scope: a single existence check on the canonical token `entity_refresh_failed_uuids` in STAGE1_SYSTEM_PROMPT — no wording, ordering, or section-title pins.
design_decisions.rationale: Per the architect rules, prose pinning of system prompts is forbidden ("documentation work, not TDD work"), but a one-line existence check on a load-bearing canonical token is allowed. The string `entity_refresh_failed_uuids` is the machine-readable contract: the next remediation cycle (Stage 2) will look for this stats key when re-attempting refresh failures, so deleting/renaming it would be a behavioural regression worth catching. This pattern matches the existing `TestStage1PromptMentionsRefreshEntitySummary` precedent (`assert 'refresh_entity_summary' in STAGE1_SYSTEM_PROMPT`) and the task 1192 reviewer feedback that explicitly rejected wording/positional meta-tests in favour of a single existence check.

design_decisions.decision: Use the plural list-typed key name `entity_refresh_failed_uuids` (not the singular `entity_refresh_failed_uuid`) as the canonical contract.
design_decisions.rationale: The task description offers both singular and plural options ("entity_refresh_failed_uuid OR appended to an entity_refresh_failed_uuids list") and explicitly recommends "append to list" in the implementation paragraph. A plural list is more robust: a single Stage 1 cycle can attempt multiple refresh_entity_summary calls (the existing `entity_refreshes_attempted=2, entity_refreshes_succeeded=2` example confirms multi-attempt cycles), so a singular key would silently overwrite earlier failures. The plural list also matches the existing prompt's discipline of accumulating per-call observations rather than overwriting (e.g. `memory_ids` aggregation, `graphiti_writes_queued` counter).

design_decisions.decision: Place the new section between the existing `## Verifying update_edge writes (Task 1145 Guard 2)` block and `## Retrospective Episodes` block (i.e. after the other write-verification disciplines, before the snapshot/temporal sections).
design_decisions.rationale: The new section is conceptually a write-failure-recording discipline — semantically adjacent to "Verifying Writes" and "Verifying update_edge writes". Placing it there groups all write-verification rules together and matches the prompt's existing topical ordering (write disciplines → temporal/snapshot disciplines → flag handling). Per the task 1192 reviewer feedback we DO NOT add a position-pin test asserting this ordering — the placement is a maintainability convenience for human readers, not a contract.

design_decisions.decision: No production code (stats_verifier.py, MemoryConsolidator, etc.) is modified — the change is system-prompt-only.
design_decisions.rationale: stats_verifier._OP_TO_STAT maps integer counters from observed write_journal ops; entity_refresh_failed_uuids is a list of UUIDs the LLM populates directly into the stage stats dict, not derived from any backend op. Adding list-typed keys to the verifier would require a separate extension (out of scope for this task per "update the Stage 1 system prompt to mandate ..."). The Stage 1 LLM agent already has full control over its stats dict — the prompt addition is sufficient to introduce the convention. Future hardening (a verifier that flags missing entity_refresh_failed_uuids when entity_refreshes_attempted > entity_refreshes_succeeded) would be a follow-up task.

design_decisions.decision: Reverse the test-scope decision recorded earlier: delete `test_prompt_mandates_recording_failed_uuid_in_stats` rather than keep the existence-check on `entity_refresh_failed_uuids`. Keep the prompt section (step-2) intact.
design_decisions.rationale: The reviewer's blocking feedback (reviewer_comprehensive: wording_meta_test) correctly points out that the existence check is a wording/meta-test: no consumer in cli_stage_runner or Stage 2 currently parses `entity_refresh_failed_uuids` from agent stats, so the test enforces a "contract" that nothing reads — only the LLM-following-the-prompt makes the section work, and a substring assertion does not validate that. This collides with the architect rule against grepping source files for "did the author mention X" strings (which is exactly what this test does). The earlier rationale (matching the precedent of `test_prompt_lists_refresh_entity_summary_tool`) is weaker than I argued: the precedent test pins an existing, already-consumed tool-name token, whereas this new test pins a token that has no consumer yet. The reviewer explicitly forbids the alternative fix (hardening the substring) because it deepens the meta-test hole. The right shape is: keep the prompt instruction (step-2 still has runtime value — it changes LLM behaviour), delete the meta-test, and write a runtime test against the future Stage 2 consumer when that consumer is built. That follow-up belongs to the task that wires Stage 2 to read the stats key, not to this task.

design_decisions.decision: Post-review correction: expand scope to include `prompts/stage2.py` (the `## Consuming Stage 1 Refresh Failures` section). Apply the reviewer's Option (b) for the get_entity pre-check (drop entirely rather than try to add a UUID-accepting variant), add `project_id` to the refresh_entity_summary example, and switch the error-model wording from 'raises' to 'response contains error field' consistently in stage1.py:141 and stage2.py:228, 235.
design_decisions.rationale: The implementation phase added a complementary `## Consuming Stage 1 Refresh Failures (Task 1157)` section to `prompts/stage2.py` (commit a8e42eb96e) so Stage 2 could consume the new `entity_refresh_failed_uuids` stats key end-to-end. That addition was within the spirit of task 1157 (the stats key is useless without a consumer) but introduced three contract bugs that the reviewer flagged as blocking: (1) `get_entity(entity_uuid=...)` — the actual signature is `get_entity(name: str, project_id: str)`, no UUID parameter; (2) `refresh_entity_summary(entity_uuid=...)` missing required `project_id`; (3) all three uses of 'raises' incorrectly describing what the LLM observes — every MCP tool returns `{'error': ..., 'error_type': ...}` instead of raising. Choice rationale per blocking-issue: (A) reviewer's Option (b) is simpler than option (a) (adding entity_uuid to get_entity) and correct because refresh_entity_summary already accepts entity_uuid directly and returns its own error response — one fewer tool call per UUID, no API surface change required; (B) adding project_id is required by the validator at server/tools.py:890; (C) the response-shape rephrase is necessary because an LLM treating `{error: 'NodeNotFoundError: ...'}` as a successful refresh would silently swallow the failure and defeat the entire task. Files list updated to add stage2.py.

steps.description: Add a new test method `test_prompt_mandates_recording_failed_uuid_in_stats` to the existing `TestStage1PromptMentionsRefreshEntitySummary` class in `fused-memory/tests/test_refresh_entity_summary.py` (around line 864, immediately after `test_prompt_instructs_calling_after_edge_deletion`). The test imports `STAGE1_SYSTEM_PROMPT` from `fused_memory.reconciliation.prompts.stage1` and asserts `'entity_refresh_failed_uuids' in STAGE1_SYSTEM_PROMPT`. Include a docstring explaining that this is the canonical machine-readable contract token Stage 2 remediation will look up, so removing the section is a behavioural regression. Run pytest to confirm the test FAILS on the current STAGE1_SYSTEM_PROMPT (the token does not yet appear). Verifies the test is genuinely red before implementation.

Add a new `## Refresh Entity Summary Failure Recording (Task 1157)` section to `STAGE1_SYSTEM_PROMPT` in `fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/prompts/stage1.py`. Place it between the existing `## Verifying update_edge writes (Task 1145 Guard 2)` block (ending around line 138) and the `## Retrospective Episodes` block (starting around line 140). Section content (using the prompt's existing line-continuation `\` style):

  ```
  ## Refresh Entity Summary Failure Recording (Task 1157)
  When `mcp__fused-memory__refresh_entity_summary` raises (NodeNotFoundError or any other \
  exception), you MUST preserve the attempted entity_uuid so the next remediation cycle can \
  target it precisely instead of recovering it heuristically.
  
  1. On any refresh_entity_summary exception, append the attempted entity_uuid to a list \
     in your stats dict under the key `entity_refresh_failed_uuids`. Initialise to a fresh \
     list on the first failure; append (do not overwrite) on subsequent failures so multiple \
     failures in one cycle are all recorded.
  2. If your stats dict is already finalised (e.g. the failure surfaces after you have \
     produced your structured-output report), emit a one-sentence \
     `add_memory(category='observations_and_summaries')` containing the attempted entity_uuid \
     and the exception type so Stage 2 can locate it via search.
  3. Continue with the remaining work — a single refresh failure does not abort the cycle.
  
  Skipping this recording forces the next remediation cycle to identify the failed entity \
  by heuristic, which costs a full reconciliation cycle to recover (cycle-46 precedent).
  ```

Run the step-1 pytest and confirm the existence-check now PASSES. Run the full `tests/test_refresh_entity_summary.py` test file to confirm no regression in the surrounding suite (especially the existing `TestStage1PromptMentionsRefreshEntitySummary` methods).

Delete the meta-test `test_prompt_mandates_recording_failed_uuid_in_stats` from `fused-memory/tests/test_refresh_entity_summary.py` (currently at lines 866-875, inside the `TestStage1PromptMentionsRefreshEntitySummary` class). The reviewer flagged this as a wording/meta-test that pins a literal substring (`'entity_refresh_failed_uuids'`) in a module-level prompt string without exercising any runtime behaviour: no consumer in cli_stage_runner or Stage 2 currently parses that key from agent stats, so the "machine-readable contract" framing in the test docstring is misleading — the contract is enforced only by the LLM following the prompt, and a substring check does not validate that.

Action: remove only the `test_prompt_mandates_recording_failed_uuid_in_stats` method (and its docstring) from `TestStage1PromptMentionsRefreshEntitySummary`. Leave the two pre-existing sibling tests (`test_prompt_lists_refresh_entity_summary_tool` at line 854 and `test_prompt_instructs_calling_after_edge_deletion` at line 859) untouched — those check distinct existing behaviours and are not part of this regression.

Do NOT add a replacement test. Per the reviewer's explicit guidance ("Don't propose hardening the substring match — that just deepens the meta-test hole") and the architect rules forbidding doc-prose meta-tests, the correct shape is: keep the prompt section added in step-2 (it instructs the LLM agent's runtime behaviour), but verify it via a future runtime test against the eventual Stage 2 consumer that reads `entity_refresh_failed_uuids` from a stats dict. That consumer does not yet exist, so the runtime test is out of scope for this task.

This is a documentation-cleanup edit, not TDD — therefore a single impl step with no preceding test step (per the architect rule that documentation/wording fixes get a single impl step).

Verification: run `pytest fused-memory/tests/test_refresh_entity_summary.py::TestStage1PromptMentionsRefreshEntitySummary -v` and confirm the two surviving tests still pass and the deleted test is gone (no collection error). Then run the full `pytest fused-memory/tests/test_refresh_entity_summary.py` to confirm no regression elsewhere in the file. The prompt change from step-2 (commit 464e751e6f) is unaffected by this revert.

Fix the three blocking review issues regarding incorrect MCP tool signatures and an incorrect error model in the Task 1157 prompt sections. This is a documentation/wording fix per the architect rules ("If a task description asks you to ... align the comment with ... that is documentation work, not TDD work. Plan a single impl step ... no test"). All three corrections land together because the reviewer asks for the error-model fix to be applied consistently across both files (stage1.py:141 and stage2.py:228, 235), and the stage2 signature fixes share the same paragraph as the stage2 wording fix — splitting would leave the prompt in an inconsistent intermediate state.

THREE COORDINATED EDITS:

(A) **Drop the `get_entity` reachability pre-check entirely** in `fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/prompts/stage2.py` (the `## Consuming Stage 1 Refresh Failures (Task 1157)` section, lines 226-237). Verified at fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/tools.py:577 the actual signature is `get_entity(name: str, project_id: str, ...)` — it accepts no `entity_uuid` parameter, and the underlying memory_service.get_entity calls graphiti.search_nodes(query=name, ...) which fuzzy-matches by name. An LLM following the current prompt would either get a parameter-validation error or silently fuzzy-match the literal UUID string against entity names. Per the reviewer's recommended Option (b), remove the pre-check rather than try to fix it: refresh_entity_summary already accepts entity_uuid directly (verified at server/tools.py:856-858) and returns its own error response, which serves as the reachability signal — one fewer tool call per UUID.

(B) **Add `project_id` to the `refresh_entity_summary` example call** in the same stage2.py section. Verified at fused-memory/src/fused_memory/server/tools.py:856-857 the tool requires `project_id: str` as a parameter and runs `validate_project_id(project_id)` before dispatch (line 890). A call with only `entity_uuid` would hit the validator and return a ValidationError dict, so the retry would never execute. The corrected example reads `mcp__fused-memory__refresh_entity_summary(entity_uuid=<uuid>, project_id=<current project_id>)`.

(C) **Switch from 'raises' to 'response contains error field' wording** in three places: `fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/prompts/stage1.py:141` (and the matching language in step 1 at line 145) AND `fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/prompts/stage2.py:228, 235`. Every MCP tool wraps its body in `try/except Exception as e: return {'error': str(e), 'error_type': type(e).__name__}` — verified at server/tools.py:615 (get_entity) and server/tools.py:908 (refresh_entity_summary). The LLM never sees a raised exception; it sees a successful response that may contain an `error` field. Without this fix, an LLM following the current prompt would treat `{error: 'NodeNotFoundError: ...'}` as a successful refresh and never record the UUID, defeating the task. Surface the recovery rule explicitly: 'A response is a successful refresh only when it does NOT contain an `error` key.'

POST-EDIT TARGET CONTENT:

Stage2.py `## Consuming Stage 1 Refresh Failures (Task 1157)` section (replace lines 217-241 with):
```
## Consuming Stage 1 Refresh Failures (Task 1157)
At the start of each cycle, check whether the Stage 1 payload includes a non-empty \
`entity_refresh_failed_uuids` list in its structured report. These are entities whose \
prior `mcp__fused-memory__refresh_entity_summary` call returned an error response in \
the Stage 1 run; they are targeted retries, not heuristic re-scans. The stats dict is \
the single authoritative channel for these UUIDs — do not search for `source_description` \
markers or other side channels, because Stage 1 does not write them and the fused-memory \
`search` API does not match on episode `source_description` anyway.

For each UUID in `entity_refresh_failed_uuids`:
1. Call `mcp__fused-memory__refresh_entity_summary(entity_uuid=<uuid>, \
   project_id=<current project_id>)` to attempt the deferred refresh.
2. Inspect the response. **A response is a successful refresh only when it does NOT \
   contain an `error` key.** On a successful refresh, add the UUID to \
   `entity_refresh_retried_succeeded` in your stats.
3. If the response contains an `error` field (commonly with `error_type` such as \
   `NodeNotFoundError`), add the UUID to `entity_refresh_retried_failed` in your stats \
   and include a note in your structured report so the operator can investigate the \
   persistently unreachable entity.

Process all listed UUIDs before beginning other reconciliation work. Each retry costs \
one tool call; skipping them forces the next Stage 1 cycle to re-discover the failed \
entity by scanning all entity summaries heuristically.
```
